referees.quote: I am unsure whether the presented research is of sufficiently broad interest for publication in Nat. Commun.. Irrespective of this, some clarifications regarding the validity of the conclusions based on the presented ARPES results are required.
I think that the manuscript needs to be supported by additional data and analysis to unarguably support their claim to have observed 'altermagnetic split bands.'
I have strong reservations against the paper being published in Nature Communications... Nature Communications may not be the right platform to disseminate the same.

note: First round is Version 0 of this Nature Communications file. Nothing indicates a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. R1 is borderline between major revision and reject. They doubt broad interest and suggest the key ARPES feature is 'most likely a surface state', but they do not reject outright and ask for clarifications 'irrespective of this', so major revision was chosen. R3 judges the work sound but unsuitable for the journal on novelty grounds, which maps to reject. None of the three referees uses the scale terms explicitly.
